issues.legal_issue: A court reviewing grants to affected private parties must address their material submissions and the issues identified on remand before canceling those grants.
material_facts: A public interest writ challenged long-term leases of government orchards, and an earlier remand directed the High Court to consider whether the government policy was lawful and in the public interest after hearing the nominees.
An affected grantee filed affidavits asserting that the policy served the public interest, that it had complied with the policy and lease conditions, and that inspections had taken place.

The High Court canceled the grantee’s grants without analyzing those submissions or deciding whether the policy was lawful and in the public interest, and relied on its analysis of another grantee’s circumstances.
Cancellation of the grants had serious civil consequences for the affected grantee.
issues.conclusion: The judgment was set aside insofar as it concerned this grantee, and the matter was remanded for fresh consideration of the grants after addressing the grantee’s submissions and the relevant policy issues.
issues.legal_principle: A decision with serious civil consequences must be supported by reasoned consideration of the affected party’s material contentions. The earlier remand required consideration of the policy’s legality and public interest and an opportunity for the nominees to be heard; that direction drew on Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airports Authority of India, (1979) 3 SCC 489, concerning public-interest scrutiny of government action. The proceeding was under Article 226; no separate statutory provision was applied to this procedural ruling.

predicates.public_interest_writ_challenges_public_a: A person brings a public interest writ challenging grants of public assets to private parties.
predicates.affected_grantee_submits_material_defens: A grantee affected by the challenge submits material factual and legal grounds in support of its grant.
predicates.court_does_not_analyze_those_defenses: The court cancels the grantee’s grant without analyzing the grantee’s material submissions.

issues.definition: When a public interest writ challenges grants of public assets and an affected grantee’s material defenses are not analyzed, the judgment is set aside and the grants are reconsidered as to that grantee.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not finally decide a public interest writ against an affected party without ensuring that the party, or appropriate successors where the party has died, had notice and an opportunity to be heard.
material_facts: The public interest writ challenged government orchard grants, and an earlier remand directed that the nominees be given an opportunity to participate.
One grantee died before the High Court ordered that grantee’s impleadment.
The High Court’s judgment did not establish when or whether service was complete, and the deceased grantee could not appear; the grantee’s successors asserted that they had received no notice.
The High Court proceeded to final disposal without hearing the grantee or the successors.
issues.conclusion: The judgment was set aside insofar as it concerned the grants attributed to the deceased grantee, and the matter was remanded for fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: A court must not finally determine a matter affecting a party without ensuring proper notice and an opportunity to be heard. Where the named party died before impleadment, the court must ensure that the appropriate successors can participate. This follows from the requirements of a fair hearing and the earlier remand direction to hear the nominees; the proceeding was under Article 226, and no separate statutory provision was applied to this ruling.

predicates.public_interest_writ_challenges_public_a: A person brings a public interest writ challenging grants of public assets to private parties.
predicates.affected_grantee_dies_before_impleadment: A grantee affected by the writ dies before the court orders that grantee to be joined as a party.
predicates.court_finalizes_case_without_ensuring_no: The court finally decides the matter without establishing that the deceased grantee’s appropriate successors received notice and an opportunity to participate.

issues.definition: When a grantee dies before impleadment and the court finally decides a public interest challenge without ensuring notice and an opportunity for the successors to participate, the judgment is set aside and the grants are reconsidered after hearing them.
